title: platform-app
description: The surround. `additionalProperties: false` everywhere it is modelled: a typo'd values key that silently does nothing is the most common Helm failure mode, and this file is the only thing that catches it (history/design/10-verification.md, "Schema validation"). Profile names and datastore names are deliberately left as plain strings — the templates already fail loudly and name the alternatives, so restating the list here would only be a second copy to drift.

baseDomain.description: Public DNS suffix, supplied as ${BASE_DOMAIN} by the app file. Required by any route using the short `host` form.

routes.description: One entry per HTTPRoute, grouped by BACKEND rather than one per path: the Envoy traffic policies attach to an HTTPRoute, and an upload path wants a body limit a websocket path must not have.

name.description: Suffix for the HTTPRoute name. Omit for the bare <app> route.

host.description: Short form: <host>.<baseDomain>, defaulting to the app. `hostname`, if set, wins.

hostname.description: A full hostname, for a host outside <baseDomain>.

deny.description: Prefixes answered 403 at the edge, ahead of `paths` and with no backendRef.

requestBuffer.description: Envoy holds the whole request and rejects anything larger — nginx's client_max_body_size.

timeout.description: Request timeout: slow is not hung.

websocket.description: No buffering, no request timeout, the long `websocketIdleTimeout`.

then.$comment: Buffering a request that never ends is how you break a websocket. The template fails on this too; the schema fails on it before anything renders.

pdb.description: Set by the size profile together with the release's replicas: the surround cannot read another release's replica count, so "a PDB only when replicas > 1" is not a decision it can make.

maxUnavailable.description: Always maxUnavailable, never minAvailable: a minAvailable PDB on a single replica blocks every drain.

components.description: PDB name suffix -> pod selector labels.

networkPolicy.description: NOT ENFORCED on this cluster: Flannel ships no policy controller (adr/0103). Emitted because the egress graph is real knowledge and costs nothing to express; never cite it as segmentation.

items.description: Exactly one shape: {datastore}, {identity: true}, {app, port}, {external: true, port}.

mediaProxy.description: The backend for the `/media` route, for an application that authorises attachments by subrequest, as La Suite's do; adr/0109 says why this pod belongs to the surround.

path.description: Must end in `/`: nginx joins it with nothing, and the view reads the real URL from X-Original-URL.

bucket.description: No default: silently proxying the wrong bucket is worse than failing.

maxBodySize.description: Caps the auth subrequest's own body, not the download. Uploads do not pass through here.

locations.description: One nginx prefix location per entry; the longest prefix wins regardless of order. `headers` are added on top of the Content-Security-Policy every location gets.

staticFiles.description: A few files served from the application's own origin, for frontends that take a URL rather than content: the switcher's scripts (apps/README.md, The switcher). Enabling it also adds the `<app>-static` route at `path`. The files come from a kustomize configMapGenerator, so they stay real, lintable files.

filesConfigMap.description: ConfigMap whose keys are the filenames to serve; default <app>-gaufre.

servicesConfigMap.description: The switcher's service list (apps/services.yaml), served in the same directory; "" for none.

extraObjects.description: Rendered verbatim. Not modelled further on purpose — this is the escape hatch, and a schema over it would be a second API.
